body.statement: Coverage accounting on the frozen sample: each symbol has 62 observed unadjusted closes (common_dates = union_dates = 62; first 2026-05-06, last 2026-07-31). A 5-observation raw return needs 6 closes per signal (close[t] plus the 5 prior observed closes), so exactly 5 warmup rows per symbol are excluded as insufficient past observations, leaving 57 eligible signals per symbol; the signal at the last observed close 2026-07-31 has no next observed close, leaving 56 signals with a next observed close. The 5 warmup exclusions must not be conflated with the 6 closes required per signal, and any change to lookback or volatility window changes these counts and needs a fresh inspection.

body.statement: Unproven hypothesis: realized-volatility normalization is motivated by observed cross-symbol dispersion. Sample SD of one-observation returns is 0.0252 for 300750.XSHE, 0.0199 for 601318.XSHG and 0.0122 for 600036.XSHG, and baseline 5-observation score SD spans 0.0279 (600036.XSHG) to 0.0428 (300750.XSHE), so dividing the trailing return by trailing daily-return SD times sqrt(lookback) might put the three symbols on a common per-unit-risk scale. This is motivation only: descriptive score differences cannot establish superiority or improved comparability, the scaled score must not be described as an annual Sharpe ratio or as removing systematic risk, and its eligibility effect (rows lacking positive trailing volatility) is unknown until the exact spec is inspected.

No forward performance labels exist, so neither direction has demonstrated benefit; trailing-return means describe the past sample only and cannot establish a winning sign, and the universe is a small convenience sample with no alpha or superiority proof.

Finding b3f155f334a27c70c322bb9c3d45dd10b892d5005057082dcc38d427ff3b0e90 motivates realized-volatility scaling as a way to pose a common per-unit-risk scale; I inspected the exact spec (inspection fa7ac498a56660868bb467035ddf39a7e9c6c8eaac9ddd28e9692f09544b2ec3, spec_sha256 4216e2638a1fd0bbfbb9b385ef2cc18a99e6208e18da8b35b3aac630c9aa6053) before adopting. volatility_window=5 is deliberately aligned with the lookback so both use the same 6 closes per signal: the inspection confirms closes_required_per_signal stays 6, warmup exclusions stay 5, additional_exclusions are 0, and coverage stays 57 eligible signals with 56 having a next observed close, so the revision adds no applicability exclusion and no extra warmup. The observed effect is a score-scale change (means -0.389/-0.282/-0.408, sample SD 1.13/1.74/1.56, 171 changed rows vs the initial inspection): this is a descriptive consequence of the transformation, not proof of improvement, superiority, alpha or removal of systematic risk, and descriptive score differences cannot establish superiority. Notably the scaled dispersion is still not equalized across symbols (SD spans 1.13 to 1.74), so even improved comparability remains unproven and is itself part of the research question for later evaluation. Direction is retained at +1 as the operator's unproven starting point: the in-sample drift evidence is mixed (negative in two symbols, +0.00076 one-observation mean in 600036.XSHG) and no forward labels exist, so choosing direction=-1 now would fix a sign on the same window reserved for later evaluation. No max_absolute_daily_return bound is added: the largest absolute one-observation return in the sample is 0.07121171770972035, and close-only jumps cannot identify corporate actions, so a return bound would be an unmotivated extra exclusion rather than a corporate-action control. Applicability follows from the cited evidence: 62 observed closes per symbol on the observed union (which is not an exchange calendar), 6 closes required per signal, signal after close t using only observations at or before t, execution no earlier than the next observed close, and the last-row signal having no next observed close. Evidence needed next, per the research contract: a separate future evaluation with forward return labels (including a direction comparison) and an out-of-sample check of whether the scaled scores actually reduce cross-symbol dispersion; none of that is demonstrated here.

model.cost_basis: Existing GLM Coding Plan Pro. The shared cash ledger retains a conservative exposure debit, not an incremental cash invoice; subscription purchase cost is not allocated. Credits are a conservative upper estimate ignoring cache and off-peak discounts, not an account invoice.
model.rate_definition: Call totals attributed to dispatch/completion, not per-token arrival. Unknown usage is excluded from TPM, counted in RPM and retains its budget reservation.

native_team_tasks.description: Inspect all frozen sources and the initial/current factor. Identify concrete source-supported constraints and separately label hypotheses. Submit up to four findings. A cited observation can motivate an unproven testable hypothesis. Absence of proven alpha does not disqualify exploration. No prescribed correction; do not invent missing data, trading results or corporate actions.
native_team_tasks.subject: reviewer-1: analyze

native_team_tasks.description: Use the recorded findings and the same full evidence to propose one defensible executable factor revision, or explicitly retain the factor if no change is supported. Inspect the chosen specification, cite exact evidence, dispose of every current finding and distinguish an observed score change from unproven improvement. An exploratory candidate is a proposal for later evaluation, not deployment or proof of alpha. Explain why its applicability or research question follows from cited evidence. You may inspect a motivated alternative without adopting it; never force a change.
native_team_tasks.subject: author-2: design

native_team_tasks.description: Review the exact current complete artifact, its executable inspection, claims, rationale, decisions and limits against the frozen sources. Report remaining issues. No performance or causality claim follows from descriptive score differences.
native_team_tasks.subject: reviewer-3: review

resources.scope: Shared guard/DSH/data process tree during activity windows, not isolated per-agent allocation. Host readings include other work. CPU intervals crossing activity boundaries and short-lived children may be missed. Null means unmeasured.
